note: Planning components for commercial buildings, built from the North American materials library and grouped by the envelope classes the energy codes use (ASHRAE 90.1 / IECC: mass, steel-framed, wood-framed, metal building; insulation above deck, attic; slab on grade). Each component is an ordered stack of library layers with published R/U sources. Walls, roofs, doors, and windows run outside to inside. Floors run top to bottom. Ceilings run from the room toward the outside. A series stack is layers in contact. A ceiling-and-roof stack is not a series path, because a plenum sits between them.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade 4 in, carpet
assemblies.typicalUse: Offices, dining rooms, classrooms, cinemas, hotel rooms
assemblies.source: Carpet with fibrous pad, R-2.08, over 4 in heavyweight undried concrete, R-0.32.
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. Soil and air films are not included.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade 4 in, tile
assemblies.typicalUse: Kitchens, restrooms, lobbies, and wet areas
assemblies.source: Tile, R-0.05, over 4 in heavyweight undried concrete, R-0.32.
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. Tile thickness was not stated in the source table. Thinset is not a separate row.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade 4 in
assemblies.typicalUse: Storage, corridors, and back of house; sealed or polished concrete
assemblies.source: 4 in heavyweight undried concrete, R-0.32.
assemblies.notes: A bare slab. Pick a floor finish on the space when it has one.

assemblies.name: Insulated floor panel on a slab
assemblies.typicalUse: Walk-in coolers and freezers, cold rooms
assemblies.source: U.S. Cooler exposed prefabricated floor, R-28 or greater, on a concrete slab.
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. The panel R is the published minimum. Freezer floors may still need subfloor heat.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade 6 in
assemblies.typicalUse: Warehouses, factories, loading areas, and gyms
assemblies.source: Heavyweight concrete at R-0.08 per inch (Energy Code Ace layer CC14), scaled to 6 in.
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. Slab heat loss is set by the edge, not by this layer sum; perimeter insulation is not modeled here.

assemblies.name: Concrete floor over an unconditioned space, R-10 ci
assemblies.typicalUse: Floors over parking garages, crawl spaces, loading docks, or open air
assemblies.source: Heavyweight concrete 4 in R-0.32, and polyiso scaled from R-7.2 per inch to about R-10. R-10 ci is the IECC zone 5 mass floor value (U-0.074).
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. Air films and the structure are not in the layer sum.

assemblies.name: Concrete on steel deck, between floors
assemblies.typicalUse: Upper floors of offices, schools, hotels, and mixed-use buildings
assemblies.source: Heavyweight concrete at R-0.08 per inch (Energy Code Ace layer CC14), scaled to 3.5 in. The steel deck adds almost nothing.
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. When both sides are conditioned this floor is not part of the envelope.

assemblies.name: Wood joist floor, plywood subfloor
assemblies.typicalUse: Upper floors of wood-framed buildings
assemblies.source: Wood subfloor 3/4 in, R-0.94 (WAC 51-11C-61015).
assemblies.notes: Top to bottom. Joists and the cavity are not layers. Over an unconditioned space, add R-30 cavity insulation (IECC zone 5 joist floor, U-0.033).

assemblies.name: Brick veneer on steel studs, R-13 + R-7.5 ci
assemblies.typicalUse: Exterior walls of offices, dining rooms, retail, and schools
assemblies.source: Face brick R-0.44, foil-faced polyiso R-7.2 per inch, gypsum R-0.45, and an R-13 batt. The polyiso thickness is scaled to the R-7.5 continuous insulation named for an IECC zone 5 metal-framed wall.
assemblies.notes: Outside to inside. Studs, brick ties, and air films are not in the layer sum. The zone 5 code maximum for this wall class is U-0.064, which is not the same as 1 divided by the layer sum.

assemblies.name: Concrete block 8 in, R-7.5 ci
assemblies.typicalUse: Exterior walls of kitchens, back of house, service areas, and warehouses
assemblies.source: 8 in CMU R-1.11, foil-faced polyiso scaled from R-7.2 per inch to about R-7.5, and 1/2 in gypsum R-0.45.
assemblies.notes: Outside to inside. An FRP or stainless finish, as in a kitchen, is not a separate thermal layer in this library.

assemblies.name: Gypsum on studs, both sides
assemblies.typicalUse: Interior partitions: offices, restrooms, storage, and corridors
assemblies.source: Gypsum board, 1/2 in, R-0.45, both faces.
assemblies.notes: The stud cavity is empty in this demo stack. Add a batt here if the partition is insulated.

assemblies.name: Insulated panel, cooler (4 in XPS)
assemblies.typicalUse: Walk-in coolers and cold rooms
assemblies.source: U.S. Cooler 4 in cooler XPS panel, minimum R-28.8.
assemblies.notes: The published panel R is the whole wall. Metal skins are not a separate row in that specification.

assemblies.name: Insulated panel, freezer (4 in XPS)
assemblies.typicalUse: Walk-in freezers and freezer rooms
assemblies.source: U.S. Cooler 4 in freezer XPS panel, minimum R-32.
assemblies.notes: Swap this onto a walk-in when the box is a freezer. Metal skins are not a separate row.

assemblies.name: Storefront or curtain wall, low-E double glazing
assemblies.typicalUse: Storefronts, lobbies, office curtain walls, and dining rooms
assemblies.source: Engineering Toolbox sealed double glazing with a low-E coating, U-0.32.
assemblies.notes: A glazed wall uses the published whole-window U-0.32. It is not a tested curtain wall, and SHGC was not stated.

assemblies.name: Precast concrete 8 in, R-11.4 ci
assemblies.typicalUse: Tilt-up warehouses, big-box retail, cinemas, and gyms
assemblies.source: Concrete 8 in R-0.64, polyiso scaled from R-7.2 per inch to about R-11.4, and 1/2 in gypsum R-0.45. R-11.4 ci is the IECC zone 5 mass wall value (U-0.090).
assemblies.notes: Outside to inside. Furring, ties, and air films are not in the layer sum.

assemblies.name: Wood studs 2x6, R-21 batt, stucco
assemblies.typicalUse: Small offices, retail, clinics, and multifamily
assemblies.source: 7/8 in stucco at R-0.20 per inch, 1/2 in plywood R-0.63, an R-21 batt, and 1/2 in gypsum R-0.45. R-20 cavity insulation is an IECC zone 5 wood-framed wall option (U-0.064).
assemblies.notes: Outside to inside. The studs are a parallel path; the layer sum overstates the whole-wall R.

assemblies.name: Metal building wall, R-13 + R-13 ci
assemblies.typicalUse: Factories, warehouses, workshops, and pre-engineered gyms
assemblies.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5, metal building wall, U-0.052.
assemblies.notes: One whole-element row: metal buildings bridge through the girts, so a layer sum does not apply. Confirm the climate zone.

assemblies.name: Insulated metal panel, 2 in polyiso core
assemblies.typicalUse: Factories, food plants, cold storage, and warehouses
assemblies.source: Polyiso at R-7.2 per inch, 2 in core, about R-14.4.
assemblies.notes: Metal skins are not a separate layer. Panel makers publish their own R per thickness; confirm the product.

assemblies.name: Acoustic partition, double gypsum, R-13 batt
assemblies.typicalUse: Cinemas, conference rooms, classrooms, hotel rooms, and clinics
assemblies.source: Four layers of 1/2 in gypsum R-0.45 and an R-13 batt.
assemblies.notes: The batt is there for sound. Studs are not in the layer sum.

assemblies.name: Concrete block partition 8 in
assemblies.typicalUse: Fire separations, auditoriums, mechanical rooms, and factories
assemblies.source: 8 in CMU, R-1.11.
assemblies.notes: Painted block, no furring.

assemblies.name: Acoustic tile below an insulated roof deck
assemblies.typicalUse: Offices, dining rooms, retail, classrooms, and corridors
assemblies.source: 1/2 in acoustic tile R-1.26, polyiso scaled from R-7.2 per inch to about R-30, and 3/8 in built-up roofing R-0.33. R-30 ci is the IECC zone 5 roof insulation named for insulation entirely above the deck.
assemblies.notes: Room side toward the outside. The plenum between the tile and the roof is not a layer, so these R-values are not one series path.

assemblies.name: Gypsum ceiling below an insulated roof deck
assemblies.typicalUse: Kitchens, restrooms, labs, and washable areas
assemblies.source: 1/2 in gypsum R-0.45, polyiso scaled from R-7.2 per inch to about R-30, and 3/8 in built-up roofing R-0.33.
assemblies.notes: Room side toward the outside. Gypsum stands in for a washable kitchen ceiling. The space above that ceiling is not a layer.

assemblies.name: Insulated ceiling panel, cooler
assemblies.typicalUse: Walk-in coolers and cold rooms
assemblies.source: U.S. Cooler 4 in cooler XPS ceiling, minimum R-28.8.
assemblies.notes: The published panel R is the whole ceiling.

assemblies.name: Acoustic tile below a metal building roof
assemblies.typicalUse: Offices and break rooms inside metal buildings
assemblies.source: 1/2 in acoustic tile R-1.26 and the IECC zone 5 metal building roof, U-0.035.
assemblies.notes: Room side toward the outside. The plenum is not a layer, and the roof row is a whole-element U-factor.

assemblies.name: Acoustic tile below a floor above
assemblies.typicalUse: Lower floors of offices, schools, and hotels
assemblies.source: 1/2 in acoustic tile R-1.26 and 3.5 in heavyweight concrete at R-0.08 per inch.
assemblies.notes: Room side toward the floor above. When the space above is conditioned this is not part of the envelope.

assemblies.name: Gypsum ceiling below an attic, R-38
assemblies.typicalUse: Small retail, clinics, and wood-framed buildings
assemblies.source: 1/2 in gypsum R-0.45 and the IECC zone 5 attic roof, U-0.027.
assemblies.notes: Room side toward the outside. The attic row is a whole-element U-factor.

assemblies.name: Insulated ceiling panel, freezer
assemblies.typicalUse: Walk-in freezers and freezer rooms
assemblies.source: U.S. Cooler freezer ceiling, 4 in extruded polystyrene, minimum R-32.
assemblies.notes: Metal skins are not a separate layer.

assemblies.name: Exposed roof deck, membrane on R-30 polyiso
assemblies.typicalUse: No ceiling: warehouses, factories, gyms, and open-ceiling retail or restaurants
assemblies.source: 3/8 in built-up roofing R-0.33 and polyiso scaled from R-7.2 per inch to about R-30. R-30 ci is the IECC zone 5 value for insulation entirely above the deck.
assemblies.notes: Outside to inside. The deck is not in the cited R table. Use this when the ceiling is the roof.

assemblies.name: Exposed metal building roof, R-19 + R-11 liner
assemblies.typicalUse: No ceiling: factories, warehouses, workshops, and pre-engineered gyms
assemblies.source: IECC commercial envelope sample, Table C402.1.4, climate zone 5, metal building roof, U-0.035.
assemblies.notes: One whole-element row; purlins bridge the insulation, so a layer sum does not apply. Confirm the climate zone.

assemblies.name: Window, low-E double glazing
assemblies.typicalUse: Offices, storefronts, classrooms, and dining rooms
assemblies.source: Engineering Toolbox sealed double glazing with a low-E coating, U-0.32.
assemblies.notes: One published whole-window value. The panes, gap, and coating are not split into separate R-values because that table did not list them. SHGC was not stated.

assemblies.name: Window, low-E double glazing with gas fill
assemblies.typicalUse: Higher-performance glazing for any space
assemblies.source: Engineering Toolbox double glazing with a low-E coating and heavy gas fill, U-0.27.
assemblies.notes: Swap this onto a window when the product is gas-filled. SHGC was not stated.

assemblies.name: Insulated metal door
assemblies.typicalUse: Entry, service, and exit doors
assemblies.source: ASHRAE 90.1-2007 default for an insulated metal swinging door, U-0.50.
assemblies.notes: One published door coefficient. The skins and core are not split out. Use the tested door label when you have one.

assemblies.name: Uninsulated hollow metal door
assemblies.typicalUse: Older service and utility doors
assemblies.source: ASHRAE 90.1-2007 uninsulated double-layer metal door, U-0.70.
assemblies.notes: Swap this onto a door that has no insulation.

assemblies.name: Solid-core wood door
assemblies.typicalUse: Interior doors: offices, hotel rooms, and classrooms
assemblies.source: Building Material R-Values table, solid-core wood, 1-3/4 in, R-2.17.
assemblies.notes: Door leaf only; the frame is not a layer.
